event_types.method: EVENT_TYPES.length, imported. `db/schema.ts:289` re-exports the same array from `@dim/contract/events`, and that re-export is what `__tests__/event-catalog-count.test.ts` imports — so this is the identical array the catalog fence counts, reached without pulling Drizzle into this script.

verify_fences.method: distinct `pnpm lint:<key>` tokens matched by /pnpm (lint:[\w-]+)/g inside the `verify` script string. Counts the fence STEPS only: `pnpm lint` (Biome), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm verify:mobile` and `pnpm build` are also in the chain and are not counted here.

lint_scripts.method: keys in `scripts` starting with `lint:`. Compare against `verify_fences`: a lint key that exists but is absent from `verify` is a fence nothing runs — `pnpm lint:ci-parity` is what keeps the two in step.

check_scripts.method: files in `scripts/` matching /^check-.*\.ts$/. Three sibling fences are written in plain JS (`check-raw-buttons.mjs`, `check-raw-select.mjs`, `check-op-controls.mjs`) and are deliberately NOT in this count, which is about the TypeScript fence corpus.

migrations.method: files ending in `.sql` under `db/migrations/`. Migrations are forward-only and immutable, so this only ever grows.

tables.method: literal occurrences of `pgTable(` in `db/schema.ts`. A call-site count, not an import: Drizzle table objects are not collected into any exported registry, so there is nothing to take `.length` of.

enums.method: literal occurrences of `pgEnum(` in `db/schema.ts`. Same caveat as `tables` — a call-site count for want of a registry.

rls_enabled_tables.source: db/*.sql + db/migrations/*.sql (declared); the LIVE truth is `__tests__/rls/*`, which reads `pg_class.relrowsecurity`
rls_enabled_tables.method: distinct table names matched by /ALTER TABLE … ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY/i over the whole SQL surface with comments stripped, minus any later DISABLE (there are none at this snapshot). This is the DECLARED count. It is not the number of tables — a table can exist without RLS — and it is not a live catalog reading.

security_definer_functions.source: db/*.sql + db/migrations/*.sql (declared); the LIVE truth is `__tests__/rls/*`
security_definer_functions.method: distinct function names whose `CREATE [OR REPLACE] FUNCTION … $$` header carries `SECURITY DEFINER`, over the whole SQL surface with comments stripped, minus any `DROP FUNCTION` by name. Declared, not read from `pg_proc`.

cron_route_dirs.method: immediate subdirectories of `app/api/cron/`. Higher than `cron_jobs`: some routes are standalone Vercel crons and some are invoked only by the daily dispatcher.

vercel_crons_declared.method: length of the `crons` array. Only these are scheduled BY VERCEL; every other job runs because `/api/cron/daily` fans out to it.

cron_jobs.method: DAILY_JOB_ORDER.length, imported. This is the registry `app/api/cron/daily/route.ts` maps over; the route itself imports `@/db` and cannot be loaded here, but the registry module has zero imports.

ci_workflows.method: files ending in `.yml` under `.github/workflows/`. There are no `.yaml` files at this snapshot; if one is added it will not be counted until this method changes.

vitest_files.method: discoverTestFiles().length, imported from the SAME module `vitest.config.ts` feeds into its `include` globs via computeTestPartition(). It walks the repo for /\.test\.tsx?$/ skipping node_modules, .next, .git, .claude, apps and e2e — so this is exactly the file set Vitest runs, not an independent glob that could drift from it.

e2e_specs.method: files ending in `.spec.ts` under `e2e/`. Playwright's own `testIgnore` drops `demo/**` and `perf/**` at run time, so fewer than this actually run in the default project.

mobile_jest_files.method: files matching /\.test\.tsx?$/ under `apps/mobile/src/`. A separate runner (jest-expo) from the Vitest corpus — `db-reachability.ts` skips `apps/` for exactly that reason.

org_capabilities.method: ORGANIZATION_CAPABILITIES.length, imported. The UI-facing `CAPABILITY_CATALOG` in `src/modules/organizations/domain/capabilities.ts` describes a SUBSET and is deliberately not the number quoted here.

kpi_descriptors.method: KPI_CATALOG_LIST.length, imported — `Object.values(KPI_CATALOG)`, which merges the queue and compliance sub-catalogs.

k_anonymity_k.method: the exported ANONYMITY_K constant, imported. A threshold, not a count: cells with fewer than K subjects are suppressed.

token_prefixes.method: CREDENTIAL_TOKEN_PREFIXES.length, imported. This array is a hand-maintained mirror of the prefixes `lib/infra/publicToken.ts` generates (that module imports `node:crypto` and exports no prefix list); `lib/observability/redact-prefix-coverage.test.ts` re-derives the true set and fails on drift, so the mirror is fenced rather than trusted.

denuncia_kinds.method: WELFARE_REPORT_KINDS.length, imported. The same array the `denuncias/nueva` step-1 form maps over.

operator_shift_hours.method: OPERATOR_SHIFT_MS imported and divided by 3_600_000. The constant is declared in milliseconds; this key is the hours a human would say.

throttle_per_min.method: `maxPerMinute` read out of the PUBLIC_TOKEN_READ_LIMIT object literal by regex. NOT imported: the module also imports `next/headers`, so it cannot be loaded outside a request. The regex demands exactly one match for the literal and one for the field, and throws otherwise.

throttle_per_hour.method: `maxPerHour` read out of the PUBLIC_TOKEN_READ_LIMIT object literal by regex, same reason and same exactly-one-match guard as `throttle_per_min`.

signed_url_ttl_seconds.method: EVENT_ATTACHMENT_URL_TTL_SECONDS and WELFARE_ATTACHMENT_URL_TTL_SECONDS read by regex — neither is exported, so neither can be imported. The generator asserts the two agree and refuses to emit a single number if they ever diverge.

projections.method: non-test `.ts` files under `lib/projections/`, excluding the shared `types.ts`. A FILE count, and the only key here that is not backed by either an import or a declaration site: there is no projection registry to import — `scripts/rebuild-projections.ts` names each replay function individually — so adding a projection module without wiring it into the rebuilder would still move this number.

service_role_call_sites.method: literal occurrences of the service-role factory's name followed by `(` in `.ts`/`.tsx` files under those four trees, excluding the factory's own module. The trailing paren is what makes this a CALL count and not an import count — an `import { … } from` line has no paren. The needle is concatenated at runtime so this generator does not match itself. Every one of these bypasses RLS by design.

canon_rows.method: total rows — counted over `rows[]` in the canon JSON, which is the source of truth its markdown is rendered from. The same four numbers appear as `fact:` markers in `docs/architecture/conventions-canon.md` and are cross-checked there by `__tests__/conventions-canon-parity.test.ts`.

canon_enforced.method: rows with status ENFORCED — counted over `rows[]` in the canon JSON, which is the source of truth its markdown is rendered from. The same four numbers appear as `fact:` markers in `docs/architecture/conventions-canon.md` and are cross-checked there by `__tests__/conventions-canon-parity.test.ts`.

canon_partial.method: rows with status PARTIAL — counted over `rows[]` in the canon JSON, which is the source of truth its markdown is rendered from. The same four numbers appear as `fact:` markers in `docs/architecture/conventions-canon.md` and are cross-checked there by `__tests__/conventions-canon-parity.test.ts`.

canon_unenforced.method: rows with status UNENFORCED — counted over `rows[]` in the canon JSON, which is the source of truth its markdown is rendered from. The same four numbers appear as `fact:` markers in `docs/architecture/conventions-canon.md` and are cross-checked there by `__tests__/conventions-canon-parity.test.ts`.
